name: Danish plug and socket (Type K)
description: Danish household earthed plug and socket: two round 4.8 mm pins 19 mm apart and a half-round (D-shaped) earth pin on the plug below them, received by an earth sleeve in the socket. Defined by the Danish national standard DS 60884-2-D1, which also admits French (type E) and Schuko (type F) socket-outlets in Denmark.

notes: The 16 A configuration rating relies on a single secondary source (confidence low); DS 60884-2-D1:2023 was not reviewed. Products seen in a collection carry 10, 13 or 16 A.
Rated voltage is not stated by a normative source and is null; products are marked 250 V.
Frequency is not stated by a normative source.
Line on the left looking into the socket with the earth hole down relies on a single secondary source (Wikipedia); the drawing follows it.
The drawing simplifies the half-round earth sleeve to a circle and its 13 mm offset to schematic proportions.
The Danish socket also accepts unearthed plugs, among them the Europlug (Type C, family 'europlug'); that mating is stored on the 'europlug' family; the Danish 2-pin plugs are not modelled.
DS 60884-2-D1 also admits type E (pin earth) and Schuko socket-outlets and the CEE 7/7 plug in Denmark; those parts belong to their own families.
A 16 A unearthed Danish plug fits Schuko sockets according to a collection site; not stored as a mating.
